name: Altstadt Kufstein
kurzbeschreibung: Kufstein's historic old town nestled below the fortress features the world-famous Römerhofgasse, painted facades, and vibrant Tyrolean hospitality.
preis: Old town freely accessible; Kufstein Fortress charges separate admission (adults approx. €14.00)
oeffnungszeiten: Accessible 24/7 year-round; shops and restaurants operate customary local business hours
beschreibung:
Overview

The storied Old Town of Kufstein (Altstadt Kufstein) nestles picturesquely between the banks of the mighty River Inn and the towering fortress cliff in the Tyrolean Unterland. Celebrated in song as the legendary „Pearl of Tyrol“, this charming border town harmoniously unites centuries of heritage with contemporary alpine culture. Due to its strategic gateway location between Bavaria and Tyrol, the town looks back upon an eventful history reflected in massive medieval ramparts, Gothic gables, and ornate merchant residences. The old town forms the vibrant centerpiece of a globally renowned cultural and recreational holiday region.

Route & Requirements

The architectural highlight of any town stroll is the world-renowned Römerhofgasse, boasting traditional taverns, elaborate fresco paintings, wrought-iron guild signs, and historic timber bridges spanning the narrow street. From the lively main town square with its Saint Mary fountain, visitors wander along Inngasse and the riverside promenade directly beside the flowing Inn. Those seeking panoramic vistas over the rooftops can reach the entrance to Kufstein Fortress via a shaded scenic stairway or the modern funicular railway. The walking paths in the town center are level, paved with smooth historic cobblestones or asphalt, making the tour effortless and comfortable for families with prams and seniors alike.

Visit & Arrival

The public town area is open year-round with free admission around the clock. High-quality specialty shops, craft galleries, and welcoming cafés invite travelers to linger throughout the day and evening. Public transportation links are first-class: Kufstein border station is a stop for frequent ÖBB and DB long-distance trains (Railjet, EuroCity) as well as regional lines from Innsbruck, Salzburg, and Munich. From the station square, the historic center is reached across the Inn river bridge in five easy walking minutes. Drivers travel via the A12 Inntal motorway (exit Kufstein Nord or Süd) to central multi-storey car parks like Kultur Quartier or Festung.

Tips

Daily at precisely 12:00 noon (and additionally at 18:00 in July and August), the famous Heroes' Organ (Heldenorgel) sounds from the fortress—the largest open-air organ in the world, whose majestic tones resonate through every alley of the old town. Combine your stroll with a visit to the historic tavern Auracher Löchl for authentic Tyrolean delicacies, or take an evening walk along the illuminated river promenade.
